text: Batch. The first batch didn't rise, so we had to start again.
Frosting. I made two bowls of frosting, and we only needed one.
Tray. I carried the cupcakes down on a big tray.
Rise. If the cake doesn't rise, it stays flat.
Leftovers. There were no leftovers, so I didn't need to bring any home.
Flyer. We had to put a flyer on every floor of the building.
Lobby. We set up a little table in the lobby.
Pre-order. Twenty neighbors made a pre-order, so we knew how many to bake.
Sophia! Is it true you sold all your cupcakes in the lobby?
Yes! We had to put a flyer on every floor, but it worked.
Lucky you. Last year my mom and I had a sale, and we had to give half of the cupcakes away.
Oh no! Didn't you take pre-orders?
No. And we needn't have made four batches. Two were enough.
This time we didn't need to guess. Twenty neighbors made a pre-order.
Smart! Next time I'll ask you before I turn the oven on.
Deal. And you don't have to bring a tray. We have plenty.
We had to start again.
I didn't need to buy any eggs.
I needn't have made so much frosting.
We didn't have to put up more flyers.
Do you want the leftovers?

Sophia, it's Ruby! I'm in the kitchen with my mom, and it's a disaster. We had to start the cupcakes again, because the first batch didn't rise. I didn't need to buy more eggs, thank goodness, because my neighbor gave me six. But I made two bowls of frosting, and we only needed one. I needn't have made so much! So, do you want the leftovers? I'll bring them to school tomorrow on a tray.
